page: Microsoft Azure L2s_v4 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. It features 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The processor is equipped with 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. It includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations. The system is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 480 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capabilities.

Benchmark results reveal a distinct performance profile. Single-core performance is strong, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2138.0 and strong single-threaded gzip compression at 31.24 GB/sec. However, multi-core and parallel processing capabilities are limited due to the 2-vCPU configuration. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is categorized as poor, and the Geekbench multi-core score of 2622.0 is weak. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block read speeds of 20.23 GB/sec and write speeds of 14.38 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET operations also fall into the weak performance tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L2s_v4 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8 and dedicated CPU allocation alongside local storage, making it a viable option for workloads requiring high memory density per core without massive parallel processing needs. It is suitable for lightweight database tasks, single-threaded data processing, text processing, and basic web serving. It is less suitable for heavy multi-threaded compilation, complex ray tracing, or large-scale database deployments due to its multi-core performance limitations.
